messages:
Mike H: thinking out loud — we should consider a controlled rewrite of the admission/queue layer to support SLO-weighted queues and smoother token-windowing. current burst leases are brittle for mixed-latency tenants.

Sophie L: agree. main goal is smoother fairness not flat cap. want per-tenant SLO weight + per-route priority.

Rahul: +1. also need clear abuse hook: when abuse signal trips we should be able to shift weight to a protective queue without touching core router logic.

Jen K: how do we draw the interface boundary between quota/lease manager and router? currently router asks lease service for tokens and blocks. that coupling made rate-cap changes risky.

Dmitri: proposal: introduce Admission Service API. router calls /admit with request metadata, gets back decision {allow|queue|reject}, expected wait eta, and optional fallback model. keep it minimal and JSON.

Dmitri: ```
POST /v1/admit
{
  "tenant_id": "acct-123",
  "route": "/text.generate",
  "tokens": 50,
  "slo_weight": 0.7,
  "risk_score": 0.02
}

200 OK
{
  "decision": "queue",
  "eta_ms": 120,
  "cost_adjustment": -0.1
}
```

Mike H: nice. that gives router a single-shot decision and keeps token accounting inside admission. also lets us implement smoothing windows and leaky-bucket per-weight.

Sophie L: two tradeoffs: (1) latency of admit RPC vs local token checks, (2) cross-region state-synchronization. we should support a fast-path local token cache for p50 workloads and fallback to admission for overflow.

Rahul: for abuse detection, admission should accept an optional signal channel (async) so detectors can nudge tenant risk_score and push to protective queues without immediate RPC churn.

Jen K: migration plan idea: keep old lease service alive as a compatibility shim. admission will subscribe to existing leases and gradually replace routes. start with low-risk read-only endpoints.

Dmitri: metrics we need: admission.decisions{allow,queue,reject} by tenant/route, queue.eta_p50/p95, admission.rpc_latency_p50/p99, and abuse.nudge_count.

Mike H: operationally also add per-tenant budget lookahead to avoid long tails. weight-smoothing algorithm should limit sudden weight swings: moving average over 1m and 5m windows.

Sophie L: ACLs and opt-outs: enterprise customers may want strict hard limits. admission should support policy semantics: hardReject vs softThrottle.

Rahul: consider eventual consistency for quota counters — strong counters are costly at scale. design for best-effort counters with reconciliation and safety caps for hardReject only when local state proves exhausted.

Jen K: test plan: canary with traffic shaping in staging -> run chaos tests that flip risk_score and simulate token-db lag -> verify graceful fallback to local deny and fallback models.

Dmitri: coding note: keep decision enums small, keep policy language declarative. we might reuse existing policy engine (rule-config) instead of new DSL.

OpsBot: deploy candidate created: admission-svc/rc-1 -> staging. watch /metrics/admission and #incidents.

Mike H: next steps: doc RFC sketch, small PoC with local cache fast-path, and a safe-mode shim to backstop the router. tagging @Sophie L @Rahul for design write-up. :thumbsup:
